appropriate: the seed-shaped dot on the i nods to the name's story, but there is no friend or character on the sheet, so 'a small friend who reads with you' needs a sentence
distinctive: a heavy rounded lowercase wordmark is the category's chunky-sans uniform (Homer, Epic); only the teardrop i-dot differs, a detail rather than a silhouette
simple: three letters and one teardrop dot; drawable from memory in seconds
legible: pip reads at once at 128 px and in the nav bars; the lone i holds as a stroke and dot at 16 px but becomes a thin sliver
adaptable: black, reversed and one-colour panels all hold, but the app tile and avatar show only a narrow i adrift in a square, weak as an icon
timeless: rounded heavy sans is a use-carefully 'Smokies' style, justified by the strategy's rounded-sans target; no avoid-list shape
universal: the mirrored panel reads 'qiq' and the rotated panel reads as other letters; the i alone could read as an information glyph
clear: unsearched: lowercase rounded wordmarks with a leaf- or drop-shaped i-dot are common across kids' and consumer apps
congruent: round, open and lowercase-led as targeted, but it drops the mascot logo type, the weight reads heavy not medium, and there is no dosed tilt
system: wordmark, small and favicon tiers derive, but the symbol is a lone i that carries little brand, so the icon and avatar feel uneven next to the lockup
